title: Stitching Heuristics & Mini-Evals - scratchpad
content:
Context: scribbling after the LongContext workshop and a quick hallway chat with Mira about how much of the visible "stitching" failure modes are actually prompt boundary heuristics vs model degradation. Trying to consolidate heuristics + tiny evals we can run in the infra sandbox.

Top-level thesis
- For many deployed long-context applications, simple deterministic heuristics (token-aligned boundaries, anchor sentences, overlap windows) + light-weight model-aware scoring (per-chunk perplexity delta, topical drift classifier) often outperform naive fixed-chunking when measured on pragmatic metrics (answer fidelity, hallucination rate, latency).
- Need micro-eval suite that is cheap (< 1k tokens per test) and shows directionally useful signal for small config changes (overlap size, truncation policy, stitch-prompt templates, use of KV prefetch)

Quick lit pinned while I think (papers to re-skim)
- "Adaptive Stitching for Long Context" (arXiv 2028) — empirical on overlap windows; key metric: false-change rate when anchor sentence repeated. Useful baseline algorithm (alg 1) for overlap=16/32 tokens.
- "Prefix-aware Chunking" (NeurIPS 2027) — uses learned boundary scorer; heavy but a good oracle to compare.
- "KV-cache eviction and semantic drift" (ICLR 2029 workshop paper) — points out how eviction causes loss of short-term facts that show as step-change in logprob at re-surface; useful analytic for KV policies.

Notes from the workshop talk
- People are trying two axes: (A) chunking heuristic (static vs adaptive) and (B) stitching prompt/template that instructs model to reconcile overlaps.
- Practical constraint: infra wants deterministic cheap operations pre-inference. Learned scorers are nicer but expensive to retrain/serve.
- Several teams reported success with tiny overlap (8-24 tokens) combined with an "anchor sentence" strategy (repeat last full sentence in next chunk) — reduces hallucination on sentence-splitting.

Heuristics bank (to test + compare)
1) Sentence-anchor stitching
   - Ensure chunk boundary falls on sentence end when possible; if not, extend forward to complete sentence or backtrack to previous punctuation. If neither within window, use overlap of 12 tokens.
   - Pro: natural language alignment. Con: variable chunk sizes -> load balancing snafu.
2) Fixed overlap window
   - Overlap size parameter O in {8, 16, 32}. Default 16.
   - Con: repeated context costs tokens and can increase latency; but cheaper than re-encoding from scratch.
3) Per-chunk drift score
   - Compute chunk-level surprisal change when reintroducing chunk with overlap vs without; if > threshold T, prefer merge or longer overlap.
   - Implementation: run light forward pass on small context (historic KV + current chunk) and compute delta in mean logprob.
4) Anchor sentence + explicit reconcile prompt
   - Template: "You saw finishing sentence: \"<anchor>\". Now continue with rest content. If contradictions, prefer most recent statements unless marked historical." (play with wording)
5) KV-prefetch for anchors
   - When overlap includes entities, prefetch their last seen KV entries to avoid eviction-induced hallucination.

Mini-eval design (cheap, reproducible)
- Core idea: create 120 test cases (mix of long-docs + dialog traces) where ground-truth answers are extractable only if stitching preserves local continuity.
- Test categories (rough):
  A) Entity continuity (40 cases) — question relies on a fact introduced earlier and re-referenced across a stitch boundary.
  B) Temporal ordering (30 cases) — events across chunks; model must not invert order due to boundary.
  C) Numerical fidelity (20 cases) — numbers split across boundary; rounding/aggregation errors detectable.
  D) Hallucination trigger (30 cases) — designed to provoke a hallucinated fact if overlap is broken.
- Evaluation metrics: exact-match extractive score, hallucination flag (binary), and a short human-check fuzz-score (0-1) for partial credit.
- Resources: each case ~600-1200 tokens total; running across 3 model variants (base, quantized, rts-fast) should fit in a few thousand tokens total per run.

Experiment matrix (initial)
- Chunking: {sentence-anchor, fixed-16, fixed-32}
- Stitch template: {none, explicit reconcile prompt}
- KV policy: {normal, prefetch-anchors}
- Models: {redwood-small, redwood-compact-q4}
- Measure latency (p95), token cost, exact-match, hallucination-rate.
- Total combinations: 3*2*2*2 = 24 configs. With 120 cases -> 2880 runs. Cheap-ish if we run on hosted-development pool with batching.

Immediate TODOs
- [ ] Convert 120 case list into JSONL. I can sketch first 30 tonight.
- [ ] Build lightweight harness to run a per-case 1-step scoring pass (mean logprob) so we can incorporate drift-score heuristic without full generate.
- [ ] Coordinate with platform: request dev pool slot for small job JIRA-ENG-7842 (Ben to own infra request)
- [ ] Prototype anchor sentence extractor (regex heuristics + nltk-ish sentence splitter) — Mira volunteered small script.
- [ ] Save results to bucket under CONFLUENCE-PL/long-context-stitching-2029 and link back.

Open questions / things to be careful about
- Determinism vs. throughput: sentence anchors introduce variable token counts; for dedicated/dedicated-reserve pools that matters for slot allocation. Maybe allow per-request SLA hint to select "balanced" vs "aligned".
- Edge cases: lists, code blocks, tables — sentence splitter fails; fallback policy should be fixed-overlap.
- When repetition causes confusion (model treats anchor as separate mention rather than continuation) — need reconcile prompt wording tests.
- Cost: overlap increases token spend linearly; need to quantify marginal cost per reduction in hallucination. Potential to only apply overlap when drift-score indicates risk (adaptive policy).

Rough implementation sketch (pseudocode)
- preprocess(doc, window_size): for each chunk boundary candidate, run anchor_extractor -> anchor
  if anchor found and length(anchor) < max_anchor_len: cut at sentence boundary
  else: cut at fixed window
- serve(request): choose chunking policy (per-cfg). When stitching, include anchor and optional reconcile template. If drift_score_enabled: run light forward pass to compute drift delta and if > T, re-fetch with larger overlap.

Notes-to-self: prompt wordings to try (short list)
- "You saw the end of the previous chunk: \"<anchor>\". Continue, and if there are any apparent contradictions, mark them as uncertain." (friendly)
- "Previous context: <anchor>. Continue the narrative. If the previous chunk mentioned facts, prefer the most recent factual claim and call out ambiguity." (more conservative)
- "Combine previous context: <anchor> and new content, then answer the query based only on the most recently stated facts." (strict)

Handy links / snippets
- Quick sentence splitter: use regex split on ([.!?]\s+) but special-case enumerations and bullets.
- arXiv examples: https://arxiv.org/abs/2901.01234 (Adaptive Stitching — re-read section 3.2 overlap tuning)
- Internal draft with dataset examples: CONFLUENCE-PL/long-context-stitching-2029

Short-term schedule (two-week sprint)
Week 1
  - finalize 120 JSONL cases
  - bench sentence-anchor vs fixed on 30 cases
  - baseline numbers for redwood-small
Week 2
  - run full 120 cases across 3 models and 6 configs
  - analyze cost/accuracy tradeoffs + produce short one-pager for PM/legal

Final thought
- If adaptive policy (drift-triggered overlap) looks promising we can fold into Optimize recommendations as a "stitching profile" — small win for lowering cost while keeping fidelity.

Random notes / fragments I don't want to lose
- possible name for reconcile prompt template family: "stitchers" or "stitch-proto-v1"
- threshold idea: T = 0.6 mean logprob drop per token? (tune on held-out)
- check how deduplication interacts: duplicates in overlap might get compressed away in some compressed-kv representations -> risk

---
End of scratchpad. Will iterate and move to shared drive notes when we have reproducible harness.
